statement: For every integer n>=1, let P_n=({1,...,n} x {1,2}) minus {(n,2)}, ordered coordinatewise, and Q_n={x>=0: sum_{v in I}x_v<=|I| for every lower ideal I of P_n}. Then sum_{x in Q_n intersect Z^(2n-1)} t^(number of nonzero coordinates of x) equals A_{n-1}(t) B_n(t), where A_r(t)=sum_{j=0}^r binom(r,j)binom(r+1,j)t^j/(j+1) and B_r(t)=sum_{j=0}^r binom(r,j)^2 t^j. This is the entire frozen original claim, with no change of statistic, hypotheses, or parameter range.
contribution: A complete proof candidate of the explicit maximum-deleted grid proposal in Athanasiadis--Chapoton, arXiv:2605.26916, Section 9.3. A change of polynomial basis gives the exact transfer half-steps a rank-one commutator. A finite boundary trace and formal Lagrange inversion reduce the count to a coefficient sum that telescopes to the two Narayana factors. Exact finite checks support the written argument; fresh mathematical review is requested, and global priority is not asserted.
